To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) increasing plant productivity increases arthropod diversity by increasing herbivores, which in turn increases the diversity of parasites and pred- ators, and (2) decreasing plant diversity increases the diversity of predators, but not herbivores, because predators are able to specialize on the few remaining herbivore species.

(1) plant diversity and plant productivity have significant, independent effects on arthropod diversity, (2) plant productivity increases arthropod abundance and species richness through its effect on herbivore abundance, (3) plant diversity has an indirect effect on the diversity of herb ivores through its effect on parasites and predators, and (4) plant diversity increases the diversity of parasites and pred- ators by increasing the diversity of herb ivores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of plant diversity on the diversity and composition and the trophic structure of the arthropods.
the effects of plant productivity and diversity on grassland arthropod diversity.
the effects of plant productivity and plant species diversity and composition on the species richness and abundance of arthropods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) plant species richness and composition affect the diversity of arthropods through both direct and indirect pathways; (2) increasing plant productivity increases the diversity of all arthropod trophic groups; (3) increasing plant productivity may increase arthropod diversity by increasing herbivores through the consumer rarity hypothesis; (4) the diversity of parasites and predator species is positively related to the diversity of herbivor- es.

plant productivity and diversity have significant positive effects on arthropod diversity, and that these responses can be explained in part by the effects of plant productivity and diversity on herbivore abundance and species richness.
the diversity of plants, plant productivity, and the interactions between herb- ivores and their parasites/predators are important factors in controlling the diversity of arthropods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diversity and abundance of arthropods in a community is determined by the diversity and productivity of the plant community.

plant productivity and diversity affect the abundance and diversity of arthropods, and that the effects of plant productivity on arthropods are mediated by changes in the diversity of plants and herbivores.
increasing plant productivity and increasing plant diversity both increased the diversity of tro- phic levels higher up in the food chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plant productivity and diversity can have strong and complex effects on the diversity and composition on arthropod consumers, but the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain poorly understood.
plant productivity is a major driver of arthropod community diversity.
plant productivity and plant diversity both have important effects on arthropod diversity.
